rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate pushes obfuscation intensity up while respecting the workload: flops-4 is a tiny (2-function, ~700B text) floating-point compute kernel where every pass is cheap in absolute terms, but aggressive control-flow rewriting in hot FP loops carries the main runtime risk. SUB and FLA get the highest SecurityGain to attack arithmetic identity and structure recovery first; IGV's DiversityGain is maximal since global variable encoding compounds well with the other passes and adds static-analysis friction at low cost; BCF keeps a moderately high RuntimeCost weight so the dispatcher loop is only applied where the feature profile tolerates overhead, which protects the tight FP loops from pathological slowdown; IBR and ICALL are held at medium intensity to add inter-block and call-site indirection without multiplying branch-mispredict and pointer-chasing costs in the numeric core; SPLIT stays low-cost and low-risk as a diversity amplifier rather than a primary defense; all CorrectnessRisk weights stay at or below 0.2 since round 1 demonstrated the toolchain handles this sample cleanly even at full coverage.
